project.title: Digital voltage source and red logic indicators
project.question: How can a switchable digital source drive gates and visible logic indicators?
project.notes:
A binary digital voltage source drives a NOT gate. Two passive indicators observe the source and its complement; a known HIGH glows red.

Expected: With DV1 at 0, IND1 is dark LOW and IND2 glows red HIGH. Set DV1 to 1 and run again to reverse them. In Continuous, live changes propagate through the inverter after its 10 ns delay.

Try: Select DV1 to choose its binary state. Start Continuous and use Live inputs to change between 0 and 1 while retaining simulation time.
assumptions: Logic indicators observe resolved 0/1/X/Z events. They add no load or drive strength, and the red glow does not represent LED current or physical brightness.
The displayed state belongs to the selected time and the current project revision. Missing or stale results remain unobserved.
The digital-only source output is a binary logic signal. Its optional voltage terminals must be enabled and wired explicitly for analog experiments.

annotations.text: Red means HIGH (1). Dark means LOW (0). Run to observe both indicators.
Change DV1 in its inspector, then Run. Continuous → Live inputs changes it without restarting.

projectSnapshot.title: Digital voltage source and red logic indicators
projectSnapshot.question: How can a switchable digital source drive gates and visible logic indicators?
projectSnapshot.notes:
A binary digital voltage source drives a NOT gate. Two passive indicators observe the source and its complement; a known HIGH glows red.

Expected: With DV1 at 0, IND1 is dark LOW and IND2 glows red HIGH. Set DV1 to 1 and run again to reverse them. In Continuous, live changes propagate through the inverter after its 10 ns delay.

Try: Select DV1 to choose its binary state. Start Continuous and use Live inputs to change between 0 and 1 while retaining simulation time.
assumptions: Logic indicators observe resolved 0/1/X/Z events. They add no load or drive strength, and the red glow does not represent LED current or physical brightness.
The displayed state belongs to the selected time and the current project revision. Missing or stale results remain unobserved.
The digital-only source output is a binary logic signal. Its optional voltage terminals must be enabled and wired explicitly for analog experiments.

annotations.text: Red means HIGH (1). Dark means LOW (0). Run to observe both indicators.
Change DV1 in its inspector, then Run. Continuous → Live inputs changes it without restarting.

projectSnapshot.title: Digital voltage source and red logic indicators
projectSnapshot.question: How can a switchable digital source drive gates and visible logic indicators?
projectSnapshot.notes:
A binary digital voltage source drives a NOT gate. Two passive indicators observe the source and its complement; a known HIGH glows red.

Expected: With DV1 at 0, IND1 is dark LOW and IND2 glows red HIGH. Set DV1 to 1 and run again to reverse them. In Continuous, live changes propagate through the inverter after its 10 ns delay.

Try: Select DV1 to choose its binary state. Start Continuous and use Live inputs to change between 0 and 1 while retaining simulation time.
assumptions: Logic indicators observe resolved 0/1/X/Z events. They add no load or drive strength, and the red glow does not represent LED current or physical brightness.
The displayed state belongs to the selected time and the current project revision. Missing or stale results remain unobserved.
The digital-only source output is a binary logic signal. Its optional voltage terminals must be enabled and wired explicitly for analog experiments.

annotations.text: Red means HIGH (1). Dark means LOW (0). Run to observe both indicators.
Change DV1 in its inspector, then Run. Continuous → Live inputs changes it without restarting.

projectSnapshot.title: Digital voltage source and red logic indicators
projectSnapshot.question: How can a switchable digital source drive gates and visible logic indicators?
projectSnapshot.notes:
A binary digital voltage source drives a NOT gate. Two passive indicators observe the source and its complement; a known HIGH glows red.

Expected: With DV1 at 0, IND1 is dark LOW and IND2 glows red HIGH. Set DV1 to 1 and run again to reverse them. In Continuous, live changes propagate through the inverter after its 10 ns delay.

Try: Select DV1 to choose its binary state. Start Continuous and use Live inputs to change between 0 and 1 while retaining simulation time.
assumptions: Logic indicators observe resolved 0/1/X/Z events. They add no load or drive strength, and the red glow does not represent LED current or physical brightness.
The displayed state belongs to the selected time and the current project revision. Missing or stale results remain unobserved.
The digital-only source output is a binary logic signal. Its optional voltage terminals must be enabled and wired explicitly for analog experiments.

annotations.text: Red means HIGH (1). Dark means LOW (0). Run to observe both indicators.
Change DV1 in its inspector, then Run. Continuous → Live inputs changes it without restarting.
